rows.name: William E. Humbert
rows.text: Greensboro William E. Humbert, 100, of Greensboro, passed away on Thursday, October 22, 2026, at Waynesburg Healthcare and Rehabilitation Center, Waynesburg. He was born September 12, 1926, on a family farm in Georges Township, Fayette County, a son of the late James C. and Vera A. Bock Humbert. Bill was a graduate of Mapletown High School and after graduation, began working at the U.S. Steel Robena Mine. In 1944, he entered the United States Navy and served as a signalman aboard the destroyer, the USS McConnell. His ship was assigned to various duties in the South Pacific Theater of World War II. In 1970, Bill left Robena to work for the U.S. Government as a Federal Mine Inspector. In 1977, he was transferred to the National Headquarters office in Arlington, Va., as a Federal Investigator. After 23 years of service, Bill retired in 1991 and he and his wife, Wilda, relocated to Greene County. Bill served as assistant treasurer, board member and deacon at the Sugar Grove Baptist Church. In addition, he served as moderator for the Ten Mile Baptist Association of Greene County. Being civically minded, Bill served as president of the Carmichaels Lions Club, master of the Carmichaels Grange No. 1389, steward of the Greene County Pomona Grange and director of the King Coal Assocation. Other memberships included the U.S. Steel Pensioners Club, Valley Lodge No. 459, F. & A. rows.name: Monna Lee Morris Johnson
rows.text: Perryopolis Monna Lee Morris Johnson, 94, of Perryopolis, passed away Thursday, October 22, 2026, in her home. Born September 12, 1932 in Perryopolis, she was the daughter of the late Harry and Mabel Dunlap Morris. A lifelong resident of Perryopolis, Mrs. Johnson was a member of Perryopolis United Methodist Church. She retired from Frazier School District, where she worked as a cafeteria manager. Monna loved to read, play various card games, was a member of the Vernon Belles card club, the former Perryopolis Travel Club, a member of the Order of the Eastern Star and Past Worthy Matron and Past member of the Daughters of the American Colonist. Most of all Monna was one of the best homemakers, always preparing and cooking for her family Sunday dinners even after cooking all week. Monna is survived by her six grandchildren, Joseph (Kelly) Johnson, Shelly (Brian) Gilmore, Harry (Ann) Johnson, Jr., Rebecca Johnson, Bethanie (Craig) Hatlapatka, Kelly (Matt) Gurgiolo; 11 great- grandchildren, Brandon, Justin, Travis, Grace, Levi, Harry, Juliann, Joelle, Courtney, Kaden, and Jaxon; and five great-great-grandchildren, with one on the way. She was preceded in death by her husband, Charles R. Johnson; three sons, Charles H. Johnson, Robert D. Johnson, Harry E. Johnson; and an infant brother, Harry Morris. Visitation will be held Monday, October 26, from 2 to 8 p.m. in the PARZYNSKI FUNERAL HOME & CREMATIONS LLC, Family Owned and Operated, 191 Liberty Street, Perryopolis, 724-736-2515,

rows.name: Ronald W. Rankin
rows.text: Point Marion Ronald W. Rankin, 72, of Point Marion, formerly of Greensboro, passed away Wednesday, October 21, 2026, in the Terrace Nursing Home, Uniontown, after a brief illness. Born in Uniontown April 17, 1954, he was a son of the late John Wesley and Ruth D. Wilson Rankin. Ron was a retired security guard at local mines, an avid hunter, and enjoyed gardening and being outdoors. His beloved wife, Mary Ann Presock Rankin, passed away June 28, 2021. Also deceased are several brothers and sisters. Surviving are his daughter, Tracy Russell of Point Marion; two grandchildren, Mariah Russell and David Russell; two great- granddaughters, who were the light of his life, Mila and Zoey Franks; a brother, John Rankin and wife Susan of Searights, their daughter, Noel and granddaughter, Jazzy; and several other nieces and nephews. The family will receive friends in the RICHARD R. HEROD FUNERAL HOME, Point Marion, Saturday, October 24, from 1 to 4 p.m. Private interment will be in the Monongahela Hill Cemetery, Greensboro, at a later date. www.herod-rishel.com

rows.name: Carole Brezovsky Rutt
rows.text: Brownsville Carole Brezovsky Rutt, 77, of Brownsville, and Mazatlan, Mexico, peacefully passed away in Mount Macrina Manor, Uniontown, Friday, September 25, 2026. She was born March 10, 1949, the daughter of John and Amelia Brezovsky of East Fredericktown. Carole graduated from Brownsville Area High School in 1967 and continued her education at California State College, where she graduated in 1971. Carole then accepted an elementary teaching position in Ft. Lauderdale, Fla., where she met and married Robert “Bob” Rutt. They later lived in Key Largo, Fla. and Boone, N.C. before moving to Mazatlan. She continued living in Mazatlan for a period of time after Bob’s death. In 2020, Carole returned to Brownsville, where she made her last residence. Carole is survived by her siblings, Mona Gavigan, Garry Brezovsky, Pamela (Dan) Sheehan, Joni (Clyde) Titler; and nieces and nephews. Carole requested no viewing or funeral services. With family in attendance, she was buried alongside her parents in Greene County Memorial Cemetery. www.skirpanfuneralhome.com

rows.name: Paula Jo Jones Zalar
rows.text: Carmichaels Paula Jo Jones Zalar, 74, of Carmichaels, peacefully passed away Thursday, October 15, 2026. She was born February 19, 1952, in Franklin Township, to the late Carl Dewey and Josephine Jankowski Osborne. On April 27, 2002, she married her husband, Jim Zalar, who survives. Paula was a lifelong resident of Carmichaels. She was a graduate of Carmichaels Area High School, Class of 1970. She then continued her education at California State College, where she earned a Bachelor of Science in Education and a Master of Education. Paula went on to become a kindergarten and first-grade teacher in the Carmichaels Area School District for 30 years, until her retirement in 2014. Teaching wasn’t just a career for Paula, it was a calling, one she truly loved; teaching defined who she was. She leaves behind generations of students whose lives were touched by both her care and devotion. Paula was a member of St. Matthias Parish at St. Hugh in Carmichaels. She belonged to the Pennsylvania State Education Association. She also served on the board of directors at Laurel Point Cemetery. Although teaching was Paula’s passion, her family was her truest love. Along with her husband, she leaves behind her son, James E. Jones (Lisa) of Carmichaels; daughter, Melissa M. Dlugos (Jim) of Windham, Maine; grandchildren, Kaitlyn Zalar, Andrew Zalar, Jackson Zalar, Cara Mai Jones, Matthew J. Dlugos, and Sophie E. Dlugos; brothers, Gary C. Osborne (Ruth), Dennis W. rows.name: John Ricker
rows.text: Uniontown John Ricker, 71, of Uniontown, passed away on Sunday, October 18, 2026, at his home, surrounded by his family. He was born in Uniontown on February 21, 1955, to the late Raymond Ricker, Sr. and Margaret Pendlebury Ricker. John was in the first class to graduate from Laurel Highlands High School. He owned and operated Ricker’s Market, in Fayette City, for over 40 years. John had a taste for adventure; a few of his expeditions were going sky-diving and scuba diving. He was a previous exalted ruler of the former Charleroi Elks Lodge 494. He enjoyed playing golf, and was in Jefferson Golf League and several other golf leagues. John is survived by two nieces, Christine Kishel and Jessica Semachko; great-nieces and nephews: Tyler Kishel, Zach Kishel, Amanda Kishel, Jacob Uhazie and wife, Haley, and Lizabeth David; and five great-great-nieces and nephews: Grayson, Hunter, Kinsley, Axel and Andy. In addition to his parents, he was preceded in death by a brother, Raymond “Tiny” Ricker, Jr.; and an aunt, Catherine Pendlebury. A memorial service will be held at the Stephen R. Haky Funeral Home, 603 N. Gallatin Ave. Ext., Uniontown, PA 15401 on Saturday, October 24, from 2 to 4 p.m. for visitation, with the funeral beginning at 4 p.m. Your personal written tributes and memories are welcome and encourage at www.hakyfuneralhome.com

rows.name: Clarence Clark
rows.text: Point Marion Clarence “Jack” Clark, 93, of Point Marion, died unexpectedly Thursday, October 15, 2026, in his home. Born in Dilliner October 24, 1932, he was a son of the late William and Agnes Lipscomb Clark. As a young man, he had previously worked in local coal mines, as well as an area handyman. In addition to his parents, he was preceded in death by his sister, Mary Jane Butcher; and brothers, Eugene, William and Robert Clark. He is survived by a local nephew, John Butcher; several other nieces and nephews and their families; and a number of friends and caregivers in the Point Marion area. Friends will be received in the RICHARD R. HEROD FUNERAL HOME, Point Marion, Monday, October 19, from 4 to 6 p.m., when a brief funeral service will begin, with the Rev. David Lee Corob officating. Private interment will be held Tuesday in the Evergreen Memorial Park, Point Marion. www.herod-rishel.com
